item.title: Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb — Sat Oct 3 — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb Exhibit: October 3 – November 6, 2026 Reception: October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Waltz of Life & Limb pairs recent sculptural paintings by artist Mercy Hawkins, with her vibrant, large-scale watercolors on paper. With this work, Hawkins seeks to answer the internal call, to encounter what the body already knows, from our own inner rhythms, heartbeat, and breath, to dancing with wild arms. Her biomorphic shapes, formed of intersecting dots, dashes, and lines, speak to a sensory play of color, light, and movement. Her imagery evokes seed pods, flower buds, or microscopic creatures, immersing the viewer in an all-encompassing perception of nature. Artist Talk: Saturday, October 17, 2-3:30 PM (Free) Mercy Hawkins will speak about the development and trajectory of several bodies of recent work, including its connection to craft. She will also explore the intersection of painting and music. Sponsored by HF Richardson Image: Mercy Hawkins, “Melting Ice”

Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Author talk by Peter Flax: Why We Ride — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.

item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. item.title: Artist Talk with Anna Von Mertens: Wonder, Familiarity, Truth, Discovery Following the Path of Attention in Science and Art — Fri Oct 2, 4:30 PM — Cruess Hall
item.description:
Grounded in quiltmaking, Anna Von Mertens creates research-based, labor-intensive work weaving together science, history, and materiality. Her talk will center on the extraordinary life of Henrietta Leavitt, a pioneering astronomer who worked at the Harvard College Observatory studying glass plate photographs of the night sky. Von Mertens’s book Attention Is Discovery (MIT Press, 2024) celebrates Leavitt’s groundbreaking discovery, foundational to modern cosmology. The hand-stitched quilts and pencil drawings Von Mertens made based on Leavitt’s work appreciate the attentive path to discovery, celebrating labor and insight. Von Mertens will examine “women’s work”: a term historically applied to both hand-stitching skills and the scientific work of the Harvard Computers — the women who worked alongside Leavitt. Surfacing themes of individuality within community and the transformative nature of repetition, Von Mertens explores meaning embedded in our daily lives.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: "The Works of Our Hands," Related in Life and Design — Fri Oct 2 — The Artery
item.description:
The Artery presents “The Works of Our Hands,” Related in Life and Design, featuring Amina Harris, Patti Harris, and Shoshana Zeldner. The exhibit extends from October 2 to 26, with the reception on Friday, October 9, 6-9 pm coinciding with the Davis Second Friday ArtAbout. The Works of Our Hands features three family members, each having distinctive art forms. Amina Harris’s unique jewelry incorporates artifacts from ancient to modern times. Amina’s recent trip to Morocco inspired this exhibit. Patti, Amina’s sister, shows her 3-dimensional collages, using industrial design, natural materials and vintage objects. Shoshana, Amina’s daughter, creates sculptures that breath with life, exploring the relationship between the body and the subtle experiences that take place within.
Source: The Dirt

UC Davis STEM Librarian, Sheena Campbell, provides information literacy instruction to undergraduate and professional students in the STEM fields, offers individualized research support, and identifies resources to enhance the library’s collections. With her background as an artist and historian, Sheena’s research interests focus on the intersection of visual culture, environmental justice, and the history of scientific thought.

item.title: Banned Books Week — Sun Oct 4 — CA
item.description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.description:

Speaker: Oliver Kreylos
Oliver Kreylos is a computer scientist researching virtual reality and computer graphics, and their application to scientific data analysis. Kreylos received his PhD in Computer Science from UC Davis. He holds master’s degrees in Computer Science from UC Davis and the University of Karlsruhe, Germany. Kreylos developed the virtual reality user interface and research applications software for the UC Davis KeckCAVES and AR Sandbox.

item.title: Zombie Bike Parade — Sat Oct 31, 4:00 AM — Community Park
item.description:
The Zombie Bike Parade Everyone is welcome at Community Park for the festival: on foot, on any wheels, in a wheelchair or powerchair, or pushing a stroller. The official bike parade is different. It rides just under five miles at a regular biking pace, so it is for bicycles (including e-bikes, cargo bikes, tandems and bike trailers) and only for riders who can keep that pace for the whole route. Helmets are required under 18 and strongly encouraged for everyone. If the parade is not the right fit, stay at Community Park: the shows, the entertainment stations and the 2:30 p.m. skydiving finale all happen there.
Source: Davis Downtown
